text:
Maya Tran: Quick heads-up — weekly KPI snapshot shows a spike in EMEA webinar-sourced leads on Friday night UTC, then a drop Sat-Sun. looks like the EMEA slice is unstable and it's skewing week-over-week numbers :confused:
Sana Malik: saw that too. suspecting timezone batching + GA4 sessionization differences. EMEA registrants are hitting registration endpoints at local evening hours, and some ingestion jobs backfill the next UTC day
Evan Cole: so dashboards that bucket by event_date (UTC) vs ingestion_date will show different weekly totals. which does our pulseboard use?
Maya Tran: pulseboard uses event_date (UTC) for cohorts; the executive weekly deck pulls CRM MQLs which use ingestion_time -> possible mismatch
Jorge Rivas: paste the cohort query you used and i'll run a compare on event_timestamp vs ingestion_time. quick guess: we have ~8-12% of EMEA leads crossing the UTC midnight boundary
Maya Tran: base query: ```SELECT date_trunc('day', event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') as cohort_day, count(distinct user_id) FROM events WHERE campaign='emea_webinar' GROUP BY cohort_day ORDER BY cohort_day;```
Leah Park: GA4 session stitching also fragments some registrations when third-party redirects are used for European partners. those sometimes land with session_start in local tz but event_time normalized to UTC later in the pipeline
Tom B: low-effort fix: add a dashboard metadata note: "cohort uses event_time UTC; CRM uses ingestion_time; expect EMEA drift near DST changes". longer term we should standardize to event_timestamp for weekly KPIs or run a parity diff
ops-bot: Data job: ga4-ingest-backfill completed 2026-03-25T02:10:12Z. rows_processed=13,400.
Evan Cole: action plan: 1) Jorge to produce parity diff (event_time vs ingestion_time) for last three launches, 2) Sana/Leah to surface top 5 partner redirects that cause session splits, 3) Tom to add dashboard metadata + a toggle to view by ingestion vs event_time, 4) Maya to update the weekly deck note
Jorge Rivas: running parity diff now. will export CSV with day-level deltas and percent change for EMEA slice. expect upload in ~25m
Sana Malik: i'll compile the partner redirect list and flag the worst offenders (they're mostly legacy tracking proxies)
Leah Park: will also sample 100 affected user_ids to check whether conversion timing shifts (converted later vs just moved to different day)
ops-bot: Calendar: "EMEA KPI timezone parity" 2026-03-25T09:30:00Z created (30m). invited: Maya Tran, Sana Malik, Jorge Rivas, Leah Park, Tom B, Evan Cole
Maya Tran: good. for execs i'll add a single-line caveat in the deck: "EMEA weekly numbers may vary ±10% due to event vs ingestion time; parity check underway." keep it short
Evan Cole: +1. if parity shows consistent bias we should switch the weekly KPI canonical field to event_timestamp to match analytics best-practice
Tom B: toggle and metadata note are low lift, i'll push a staging change today and ping you after QA
Jorge Rivas: CSV uploaded to marketing assets: https://redwood.internal/files/emea_time_parity_329876.csv :file_folder:
Maya Tran: thanks team. this feels different from normal attribution talk (it's time-bucket noise). once we confirm parity we'll update the weekly template and add a one-line runbook for webinar ops to avoid DST/redirect surprises
Sana Malik: will add redirect checklist to the webinar playbook and surface to GTM ops
Evan Cole: great. meet at the parity sync. :thumbsup:
